articles.title: Music Assistant opens a Marketplace for music sources, speakers and plugins
articles.dek: One page finds music sources, speakers and plugins, with suggestions based on the listener’s setup.
body: Music Assistant adds a Marketplace in Settings for browsing and adding music sources, speaker support, metadata services and plugins. A Discover page puts suggested additions first, including speakers found on the network and services that fit an existing setup. Each suggestion explains its reason and can be dismissed.

Administrators can also enable the community catalog proposed on November 13, after confirming its own-risk warning. Contributions maintained outside the server then appear alongside the built-in choices, with named maintainers, source links and help destinations. The catalog remains off by default, and no existing provider has moved into it yet.

Installed community contributions can be updated individually, together or automatically when nothing is playing. The interface identifies updates that need a restart and explains blocked or unavailable contributions. Turning the catalog off requires removing what was installed from it first.

articles.title: Home Assistant’s voice preview gives missed wake words a second chance
articles.dek: Recorded tests catch more real wake phrases and lose fewer first words, with a tradeoff in similar-sounding phrases.
body: Home Assistant’s experimental Voice Support work tackles wake phrases that go unanswered and commands that lose their first word. Michael Hansen adds a second opinion when the initial verifier rejects a possible wake phrase, and places the start of speech recognition at the detected end of that phrase. Home Assistant also enables the buffered-audio request left off in yesterday’s preview coverage, but only when Voice Support can verify every active wake word.

Hansen’s measurements use 6,188 recorded audio streams from four speakers, including two children, run through Home Assistant’s voice pipeline. Among wake phrases the detector had already caught on the measured channel, one child’s verification rate rises from 28.2% to 88.1%. There is a cost: 21.9% of synthesized similar-sounding phrases that triggered the detector pass verification, compared with 10.1% before.

In the same recorded evaluation, speech recognition loses the command’s first word in 23% of accepted wake phrases, down from 30%. The work also fixes a canceled verification leaving its answer behind for the next request. These are preview results: the app has not been tested on a real device, and its ARM64 images have not been tested.

pullRequests.title: Second opinion and speech-to-text boundary from Parakeet's CTC head

articles.title: ESPHome avoids a reboot burst that can restart access points
articles.dek: ESP32 devices leave Wi-Fi before restarting, addressing a failure observed on a WPA3 network.
body: ESPHome disconnects ESP32 devices from Wi-Fi before they restart. Previously, shutdown could repeatedly send the same protected disconnection message, triggering a bug that occasionally restarted the contributor’s access point. A device rebooting every fifteen minutes after its Home Assistant connection was disabled exposed the problem.

Miguel Angel Nubla tested forced and safe restarts on an ESP32-C3 using ESP-IDF and WPA3. The corrected build sent one disconnection message per restart, apart from ordinary retries, and the access point stopped reporting replay failures. Other ESP32 variants, Arduino builds and deep sleep were not tested. This is Nubla’s first contribution to ESPHome.

articles.title: Music Assistant gives tracks an estimated energy level
articles.dek: A one-to-ten score appears beside tempo and musical key, with an optional table column.
body: Music Assistant adds an estimated energy level to analyzed tracks, giving listeners another way to compare how energetic music sounds. The score appears in the audio-analysis panel beside tempo and key, and in an optional Energy column that starts hidden.

Marvin Schenkel combines the track’s existing brightness, loudness and arousal measurements, so already analyzed tracks need no new analysis. The score is an estimate: a track without a proper loudness measurement can read about one level too low until that measurement is made.

articles.title: Music Assistant lets other apps take over its speakers
articles.dek: AirPlay receivers leave their groups cleanly, and stopped WiiM members can keep another input.
body: Music Assistant releases an AirPlay speaker when playback stops, instead of leaving its output reserved and blocking another music app. When an iPhone or other sender takes over, the speaker goes idle in Music Assistant and leaves its group instead of being pulled back automatically.

A related change lets a WiiM member leave a Squeezelite group when its own app stops it or switches inputs. The other speakers keep playing. That exception does not cover a WiiM leading the group or a fixed Sync Group, whose membership stays unchanged.

articles.title: Music Assistant colors its visualizer from album artwork
articles.dek: Separate controls adjust the whole picture and the waveform, replacing the flat tint.
body: Music Assistant’s MilkDrop visualizer uses the playing track’s artwork palette inside the visual effects, replacing a flat color overlay. A strength slider controls recoloring of the picture, while a separate switch applies colors to the waveform and borders.

The new controls appear in settings and the player menu. Recoloring starts at 75 percent and waveform coloring starts on; an earlier choice to disable the old tint is not carried over. Jozef Kruszynski connects the new artwork controls with the matching server change.

articles.title: ESPHome’s CC1101 radios receive longer messages
articles.dek: A larger receive limit accommodates wireless-meter transmissions that exceeded the old 64-byte ceiling.
body: ESPHome extends CC1101 packet reception from 64 bytes to as many as 1,024. Makers can also calculate a packet’s length from its opening bytes, allowing protocols whose message size is not known in advance.

Hajo Noerenberg verified fixed-length messages up to 140 bytes and a complete 194-byte wireless M-Bus frame on an ESP32-C3. The work supplies a radio capability needed by his separate meter-reading component; it does not itself add automatic meter discovery. Long-packet configurations are receive-only and do not support the radio’s hardware checksum option.

pullRequests.title: [cc1101] Add long packet support, plus a lambda packet_length for unknown-length packets

articles.title: Mi Smart Safe reports a closed door correctly
articles.dek: The Bluetooth library also infers relocking from a closed door and stops displaying an invented battery voltage.
body: The Xiaomi Bluetooth library corrects the Mi Smart Safe Box’s door readings. The safe could alternate between closed and open while remaining shut because its periodic status used the opposite mapping from its door event.

Vladimir Bely checked the advertisements from a safe running firmware 2.3.1_1160. The library also marks it locked when the door closes, since the safe sends no separate lock event, and keeps fingerprint-match events from overwriting the correct key identifier. It retains the reported battery percentage and removes the voltage estimate. This is Bely’s first contribution to the library.

pullRequests.title: fix: correct door and lock state, drop voltage for loock.safe.v1

articles.title: Squeezelite groups start and pause together
articles.dek: Music Assistant adopts coordinated timing and routes a speaker’s own controls to the group.
body: Music Assistant coordinates Squeezelite group starts and resumes using the synchronization logic from Lyrion Music Server. It corrects timing drift during playback and brings slow-starting outputs back into line at the first check, rather than waiting for a second confirmation.

Play and pause from a speaker’s remote, screen or own app also control the whole group and its queue. Previously one member could pause alone, leave the rest stuttering and return seconds behind. Squeezebox pause commands now honor an explicit pause or resume request instead of guessing from the server’s last known state.

articles.title: ESPHome curbs memory exhaustion from repeated web requests
articles.dek: Realtek and LN882x devices release closed connections sooner instead of retaining them for two minutes.
body: ESPHome prevents short web requests from piling up closed connections in memory on Realtek RTL87xx and LN882x devices. A flood of requests could exhaust the heap and restart the device; the connections are now released after about a second rather than 120 seconds.

In J. Nick Koston’s tests, 600 requests at roughly three per second previously held about 60 KB on a BW15 board. With the correction, memory on the BW15 and LN882H stayed within about 2 KB of idle and recovered in one to two seconds. Beken devices already used the shorter wait. Separate failures caused by very large request headers remain outside this correction.

pullRequests.title: [libretiny] Free closed TCP connections after about 1 s instead of 120 s

articles.title: Music Assistant skips MP3 tags that can exhaust host memory
articles.dek: Library scans skip unusually large metadata before it can consume the host’s memory.
body: Music Assistant checks an MP3 file’s metadata size before scanning it, skipping files whose ID3 tag exceeds 32 MiB. Three files with roughly 154 MiB of metadata each had repeatedly exhausted memory on a 4 GB Home Assistant host.
The check reads the small tag header first and reports an ordinary file error for oversized metadata. It prevents the audio-inspection tools from loading the full tag during a library scan.

pullRequests.title: Reject oversized ID3 tags before scanning local audio files

articles.title: SilverCrest remotes can trigger Home Assistant automations
articles.dek: An infrared receiver turns five fan-remote commands into distinct events.
body: Home Assistant’s SilverCrest Infrared integration adds a way to react when someone presses the physical fan remote. With a configured infrared receiver, it emits separate events for power, speed, oscillation, mode and timer commands, giving automations a specific button press to respond to.
A receiver-only setup can listen without an infrared emitter. The events identify matching remote commands rather than confirming the fan’s current state.

articles.title: A new guide puts AI answers to work in automations
articles.dek: Home Assistant documents probabilities, choices and scores, with a doorbell example.
body: Home Assistant’s new guide to the existing AI Evaluate action shows how an automation can ask questions about text, structured data or a camera snapshot and use the answers in its next step. Questions can request an estimated yes probability, a choice between named alternatives or a score against an ordered set of criteria.

The worked example evaluates a front-door snapshot when the doorbell rings, then thanks a delivery driver through the doorbell speaker if the model’s estimated probability reaches 90%. That number is the model’s estimate, not a guarantee. The example needs a camera, an AI task entity that supports evaluation, and a doorbell capable of the required text-to-speech playback. The guide covers both the automation interface and YAML; the AI entity must support evaluation, which is separate from data generation.

pullRequests.title: Document the ai_task.evaluate action

articles.title: ViCare measures heat delivered to rooms and hot water
articles.dek: Heat-pump output gains a live reading and separate daily totals.
body: Home Assistant’s ViCare integration adds three readings for heat-pump output: current heat production in kilowatts, heat produced today for space heating, and heat produced today for domestic hot water. The daily totals measure delivered heat in kilowatt-hours.

That split makes the heat going into rooms distinct from the heat going into hot water. Home Assistant’s statistics provide longer-term history rather than adding separate week, month and year entities.
